title: AIDA completion record
description: On what grounds one task closed, at <task folder>/completion/completed.json (ideal/completion.md, 'The completion record'). One file per task, in its own folder beside review/, because implementation's own `restart` archives implementation/ whole and this record has nothing to do with a build restart. Written once, by `close`, after the pull request body and before the task skill's `complete` writes the state. A record beside a task still in progress is a close that failed at its last step, and running `close` again is the repair. Every field is required, because one action writes them all at once. The task state says closed; this record says on what grounds, by whom, and what was left behind. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

takenAt.description: The UTC date this record was written, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed by hand.

task.description: The task's own id, read from task.json. Joined on, never re-minted.

reviewVerdict.description: What review/review.json said when the task closed, copied from its `verdict`. Four words, because a review that never ran (`none`), one that did not close (`unfinished`, a record with no verdict) and one that failed are three different facts. Only `passed` closes the task with nothing asked; every other word closes on a person's recorded reason.

closedBy.description: Who was present when the task closed. `person` on an interactive run. `nobody` on an autonomous run, which closes only on a passed review, since a script inventing a reason would be a bypass.

reason.description: The person's own sentence saying why the task closes without a passed review, given through --reason. Empty when a passed review closed it. It is not a bypass flag: a later reader learns the grounds from it.

followUps.description: One row per finding in the review record carrying `disposition: follow-up`. The task id comes from the folder check under tasks/, null when none exists, and the reason from --leave. A high severity finding with no task and no reason refuses the close, because leaving a queued security fault ships it. Empty when the review raised no such finding, or when no review ran.

finding.description: The finding's own id, as the review record carries it. Joined on, never re-minted.

task.description: The id of the task created for this finding, `<source task>-<finding id>`, when that folder exists under tasks/. Null when none does. No task field records the link, and no goal text is parsed: the folder is how completion knows the task exists.

reason.description: Why this finding was left without a task, in the person's own words from --leave. Empty when a task exists, or when the finding is below high severity and nobody said why.
